newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Unlinked bonds 1 pct of foreigners' Israeli assets.
newsitem.headline: Unlinked bonds 1 pct of foreigners' Israeli assets.

text.p: The Bank of Israel said on Monday that Israeli Treasury bonds not linked to the consumer price index represent less than one percent of all assets held by foreign investors.
The central bank said the figure showed that foreigners had not been influenced by the interest rate differential between Israel and abroad.
"This phenomenon is especially noteworthy given the marked expansion in foreign currency credit taken by foreigners in this period," the central bank said.
"This reluctance by foreigners to increase their exposure to exchange rate risk in Israel indicates they have different estimates of these risks than Israeli residents."

The Israeli private sector has been responsible in the last two years for a massive inflow of foreign currency into the country as it took advantage of high domestic interest rates to take out foreign currency and foreign currency-linked loans.

Critics of the Bank of Israel's restrictive monetary policy have contended that the inflows had caused the Israeli currency to become overvalued. Interest rates were cut sharply at the end of June, which was a factor in the Israeli shekel's recent depreciation.
The central bank said foreigners held just $340 million in government securities at the end of April, representing less than one percent of all government bonds traded on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.
"Despite the fact that more than five years have passed since permission was widened for foreign residents to invest in government bonds, their activity in the market is small," the bank noted.
